newsitem.title: USA: Mass. water clean-up needs state matching funds.
newsitem.headline: Mass. water clean-up needs state matching funds.

text.p: Officials from Gov. William Weld's administration outlined a plan to legislators that would help Massachusetts communities clean up their drinking water supplies, State House News reported.

Under the federal Safe Drinking Water Act, Massachusetts is eligible to receive $200 million from Washington over the next 7 years for water improvement and treatment. But the state must match 20 percent of the funds.
The state's Natural Resources Committee was considering a measure to authorize the $40 million in state matching funds and set up a revolving fund for drinking-water projects in cities and towns.

Secretary of Administration and Finance Charles Baker said he had worked closely with Ways and Means staff and determined that "the capacity is here" financially. If the bill passes, Massachusetts would make the $40 million available between this year and 2003.
In order to be eligible, Massachusetts must have the revolving fund in place by September 30.
Secretary of Environmental Affairs Trudy Coxe told the legislators, "Massachusetts is one of the neediest states in the country" in terms of its drinking water supply.
Coxe and Baker stressed the need for quick action by the committee, in order to get the bill signed by the September deadline.
But Rep. Forrester "Tim" Clark (D-Hamilton) asked why a time-sensitive bill was filed so late.
"If it's so important, why is it suddenly arriving on our desk?" Clark wondered.
Baker said extra time was needed to confer with Ways and Means staff and House and Senate leadership.
